utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today, we are Thursday, the 25th of September, 2008. I would like to greet the representatives of the OTP: Ms. Dahl, Mr. Mundis, as well as their legal assistant; Mr. Seselj, as well as Mr. Seselj's associates; and I would like to welcome the new members on his team, who have just taken up their new job. So I would like to welcome them. Let's resume our proceedings. We shall drop the blinds, since the witness has been granted protective measures. Before we do that, Mr. Seselj, I think you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, just very briefly, Judges. It is with great regret that I have to inform you that probably this is the last trip of my legal advisers to The Hague because this morning the Registry referred [as interpreted] to cover their travel expenses; that is to say that they are covering their own expenses here. I haven't got the money to pay for them, either, so they won't be able to come anymore. Until now, they came about once a month, and the Registry paid only for their trip and nothing else. Now they've even refused to do that, so they will no longer be able to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have been advised of this. I believe that this is something that can be dealt with. The Registrar has asked your legal advisers for a number of answers to their questions. I believe that the answers do not match the questions. This is what I have been told. There's no reason, of course, for your legal advisers not to be reimbursed their expenses, all the more so for the new arrival on your team, so this cannot apply to your new counsel. This is not something that concerns him; i.e., the questionnaire that has been sent out. Rest assured the Trial Chamber will resolve this issue so that no one is prejudiced. Let's bring the witness in now. Ms. Dahl, you have 15 minutes left. Are we going to hear the witness in open session or in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I will be needing to discuss some records that are under seal, and I also have a housekeeping matter that I realised last night when I was looking at the binders that were distributed for a particular set of records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Good morning, Witness. You may sit down. Let's move into closed session, or can you address your housekeeping matters in open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: This concerns records under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, closed session, please, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Trial Chamber would like to put the following question to you: You gave a statement to the OTP in which you indicated that you had been the victim of a number of assaults on certain dates. I shall not address this in detail. It so happens that we discover now that a serious assault that led to grave bodily injury was conducted against you, and this is something you did not mention to the OTP. Why was this assault never mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally, I did not feel it was necessary, although this was grave bodily injury. I went to see a doctor

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). Well, now people know about this incident, and I didn't really want that to happen. That would have made it an even more aggravating circumstance in terms of what had happened there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we redact at line 24 on page 29, please. Right, so you have given us your explanation. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: We also need the place of medical treatment, as well, in line 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is very tricky to switch from open session to private session, so let's move back into private session so that we can finish with this series of questions. Registrar, please, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Could we ask that the witness and the accused be reminded to allow for interpretation and leave a pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already mentioned this. Please be careful. You speak the same language, and the interpreters are having a hard time. Please proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirm, sir, that it was in July and June 1992 that the largest group of people arrived in Hrtkovci from Grubisno Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's where they came from, from Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm intentionally referring to Grubisno Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Seselj needs to be reminded to turn off his microphone to preserve the protective measures in place when he completes his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why? I haven't quite understood why. Why does he need to close his microphone to abide by the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The voice distortion works through the witness's microphone, and his undistorted voice can be transmitted through the accused's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this technical clarification. Mr. Seselj, when you put the question, please turn your microphone off. If you don't turn your microphone off, one can hear the witness's voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember - you stated that yourself, after all - that the largest number of Serbs who had arrived were from Grubisno Polje, and then you referred to Pakrac and you referred to Okucani, but most of them came from Grubisno Polje, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me that that's where they mostly came from and also from the area surrounding Zdenci. However, I have some names of persons written down who are from Grubisno Polje, so they said that most of them had come from Grubisno Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in Grubisno Polje, there was never, ever any fighting, any combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these people were brutally expelled by the Croatian Army and police without having rebelled against Tudjman's regime at all; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, but I believe you that that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know - I assume that you'd have to know - that the media in Serbia kept broadcasting the numbers of Serbs who had been expelled from Croatia before the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know what the truth was. Some say one thing, and others say the other thing. I as a person, as a human being, and (redacted), I feel sorry for the Serb people and the Croatian people on account of their suffering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I do believe you that you're sorry, but I need to establish the facts or to establish that we do not agree on the facts. So is it not a fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Registrar, we will have to redact line 15. Witness, when you answer in the future, never refer to who you are. Otherwise, we will have to redact the transcript. So don't refer to this, please. We are currently in open session, and it's rather complicated. Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have lived in that area, you weren't limited only to Hrtkovci; you went to other villages, to other parts of Vojvodina, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it obvious to you that a large number of Serbs had arrived not only in Hrtkovci but throughout Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I know that Novi Slamkamen, Golubinci, and then in Kukujevci, Gibavci [phoen], so that is to say in almost every town in Vojvodina and Srem, there were refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were several hundred thousands of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I met quite a lot of them in Sremska Mitrovica. The greatest number was there, but also in Ruma and in other villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the war hadn't started yet, and there was a huge number of refugees in Serbia. So what would be more natural than for those refugees to attempt to find somebody that they could exchange their property with so that they could have a more or less normal life? Wouldn't that be a normal conduct under the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a normal conduct. You're quite correct. I would have done the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Providing there were no incidents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, without incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was happening in relation to the exchange of property --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if I understand you correctly - because the Prosecution had not highlighted this and Mr. Seselj has just emphasised this - before the Croats left your area, I believe - and this is what I understand now - that hundreds of Serbian refugees arrived massively in the area, and you gave us the names of these settlements in chronological order. The Serb refugees arrived first, and then the Croats started to leave. Is this in the right chronological order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, the Serb refugees came. Later on, I heard that six or seven Croatian families left during the same time, and, well, perhaps they came across each other on the road. Perhaps they were motivated by fear, but it was first the Serb refugees from Croatia who came to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is now on the transcript. According to you, the Serb refugees arrived first, and they came from Croatia. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these Serb refugees who had left their property in Croatia, who were expelled, they were looking for some Croats who would be willing to exchange property, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have information indicating how many properties were exchanged between Serbs who had been expelled and Croats in Hrtkovci from June 1991 until the 6th of May, 1992, when the rally of the Serbian Radical Party was held? How many properties had been exchanged before that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, that's not my job. I don't like to interfere in other people's business. I have no information to that effect. I later on learned about this in 1995 and 1996 when we socialised in Zagreb and so on. It was then that we informed each other about these events. Now, as to who was exchanging property with whom at that particular time, I knew nothing about it then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if you don't have accurate information about the number of properties exchanged, would you agree that a large number of properties was already exchanged in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before your public rally in Hrtkovci, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's a very important piece of information for me. So a large number of properties had already been exchanged before I even appeared in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that you are aware of the fact that before my arrival on the 6th of May, there was no branch office of the Serbian Radical Party in Hrtkovci at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there were existing authorities of Mr. Milosevic. They mentioned the Serbian Renewal Movement, and then I know that there were supporters in your political party there, but I didn't know much about political parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you should know that the Serbian Radical Party was established more than a year later after other major political parties in Serbia, correct? We were registered in March of 1991. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I read it in the papers. I used to read papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And before the 6th of May, 1992, we didn't manage to establish a branch office in Hrtkovci. The ruling party, the Socialist Party, was already there, the Serbian Renewal Movement was there, perhaps even the Democratic Party of Croats in Vojvodina led by Tonkovic, but there were no Radicals there in Hrtkovci; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know about other people, and if you say so, you're probably right about what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, at this stage of the proceedings you have just said something which caught my attention. You said that you read the press at the time. We don't have the press. I assume that when these thousands of Serbs left Croatia, articles must have been written in the press about these flows of refugees. I assume that the journalist that wrote about these migrations must have also mentioned a similar phenomenon, i.e., the departure of the Croats. I assume that the journalists also mentioned that the Serbs arriving from Croatia had accommodation problems and that some of them had to buy flats or houses and that others had to turn to the authorities to have somewhere to live, and the others may have exchanged flats with Croats so that the Croats could go to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: (redacted); it's very difficult, as I have said - and you are someone who reads books. Now, could you tell us whether this was mentioned in the press? And this is irrespective of any political party intervention.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... informed about this at length, but there were so many refugees coming in from Croatia that it was absolutely impossible for all of them to fit in Hrtkovci, even if everybody had moved out voluntarily, and I regret the fact that these refugees had to go to other villages. They were overflowing to other villages, and wherever they could, they found various arrangements to either legally occupy certain houses, or in some cases they would use force to expel previous tenants. But there was a huge number of friends coming in from Croatia. I was surprised that so many people had decided to take this historic step and go into an unknown. One had to have faith to do something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to have a break now because it is 10.00. We shall have a 20-minute break and resume in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. We're in open session. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Before we resume the cross-examination of the witness, Your Honour, I wanted to report on my attempt to review and evaluate the material that Mr. Seselj disclosed to the Prosecution at the beginning of the session today. First, I want to put on the record that at 9.20 this morning, I was handed another 20 pages of material, and awaiting me after the break were an additional six pages or so of newspaper articles. I arranged to have a language assistant meet me at the break. We attempted to review the material. I was not able to get past the first couple of pages. Site translation is time-consuming; and regardless of the first read, I am unable to, within the time provided by the Defence, make a considered evaluation of the material. I was not able to read more than the first cover page of the very first document that was first presented. I propose as a remedy that Mr. Seselj be precluded from using the documents during cross-examination. I think the Prosecution is unfairly prejudiced by untimely disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that Mr. Seselj intends to use these documents. According to the case law and jurisprudence of this Trial Chamber, these documents will not be admitted. This is the way things were decided. When documents are not translated, they cannot be admitted. However, Mr. Seselj may ask questions and present the documents. On your hand, you can ask additional questions after the examination-in-chief [as interpreted], and we will ask the witness to come back for these additional questions because then you will have had time to read the documents. So let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The arrival of several hundred thousand of Serbs expelled from Croatia had to stir up anti-Croatian sentiment among the Serbian public; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that atmosphere could be observed in all parts of Serbia; that's quite logical, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amidst that sentiment, from time to time there were certain incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Serbs who were arriving, in addition to trying to find Croats that wanted to exchange their properties, they frequently came across vacant houses of people who had lived abroad for many years prior to that, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but there were such cases. As to how many, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no need to talk about figures. We're just talking about a phenomenon. So it was quite natural that if there were a certain number of vacant houses in Hrtkovci, the owners of which lived in Germany or they moved out to another place due to their work and they kept a house in Hrtkovci as their country home that they visited only occasionally, there were cases when people entered these vacant houses, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whenever somebody intervened, the police would come and evict people from those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about evictions. I did not attend them, and I don't know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can confirm that police evicted people from houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were cases when owners did not react to somebody occupying their house, either because they were abroad or because they thought it was not humane to react under those circumstances, and then police would not intervene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police would only intervene if somebody reported that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So only if an owner reported that, the police would go and evict people. Thank you. Thank you for these truly sincere answers. You know that in law, there is something called "vis maior." If there are some catastrophes, natural catastrophes, earthquakes, fires, or wars, when there is great destruction, people need to be provided with accommodation, with housing. They need roofs over their heads, and if somebody's property is available, it can be temporarily given to somebody who truly needs it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but people could live together. There need not have been any expulsions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, speaking of expulsions, do you know of any case where a Croatian family was expelled from Hrtkovci without exchanging their property with Serbs prior to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many of them who had to leave in great haste. They would only collect their passports and very few belongings, and they would leave. I heard that later on, fortunately, there was a better outcome. They managed to find better arrangements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know about these cases of people leaving in haste, but would you agree that all Croats who'd left from Hrtkovci, be it in 1991 or later, exchanged property with Serbs who had previously been expelled from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that, and it wasn't within my domain. There were authorities in charge of that. All I know are the documents that I was duty-bound to issue. I did not meddle into anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know of a single case where somebody was left without their property, that they were deported, expelled from Croatia -- from Serbia --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- from Serbia, and that their property was confiscated, and that this is how it remained? Do you know of a single such case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally don't know of such cases, but people are saying that many of them were defrauded. When they came to Croatia to the address given to them, they found people living there, which is to say that wrong addresses were given to them, and that was the greatest stress for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us understand each other. When Serbs were leaving Croatia with a Yugoslav passport, they had no opportunity to return back to Croatia, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that Croatian authorities would let in only Catholics, Croats with a Yugoslav passport, those in possession of a certificate from a Roman Catholic church that they were proper Catholics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how they arrived. I don't know how Croatian authorities conducted themselves at the border. What I was asked to do, I did that, simply that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that a large number of Croats, prior to exchanging property with the Serbs who were expelled, first went to Croatia to see the condition of the Serbian property there to assure themselves of the value of that property, and then they would come back to Serbia and sign a contract on exchange, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were cases where people would travel together to Rijeka, to Kraljevica, to make arrangements. There were such cases where they would see the property first and then exchange it. That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Serbs from Croatia were expelled in three great waves? The first wave was in 1991, and they were expelled from places where there was no war, Croatian cities such as Zagreb, Rijeka, Bijelovar, Sisak, Grubisno Polje -- it's not a city; it's a village. Is it true that before the war, it was first the so-called urban Serbs that arrived from that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether those were urban Serbs or rural Serbs, I don't know, but they were certainly predecessors who wanted the Croat families to leave their properties because they themselves needed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the second wave was in December of 1991 when there was an exodus from Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More and more people would come. Where they were coming from, I don't know, but there were many of them who came in several instances. That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the third great wave was after Operations Flash and Storm in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, we, people of Croat ethnicity, suffered greatly there, at least mentally, under pressure. We all remember the Flash and the Storm operation, but the question is, why were we, people in Hrtkovci, blamed for that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly you can't be blamed for Flash and Storm, but we have already agreed that there was an anti-Croat sentiment that surfaced as soon as that first great influx came from Croatia of several hundred thousand, and that sentiment could not be simply terminated on its own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This bad sentiment could be felt from the Serbs, and the Croats had to leave because of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I am interested in the two first waves, not the wave of 1995 but the two first ones. Did you actually talk with a Serb that would have been expelled from Croatia? Did you have the opportunity to talk to them, or was there absolutely no dialogue with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't really like to socialise with people I don't know. That is a question of my own nature, so I really avoided people I didn't know. Forgive me for my weakness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, as a Croat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I asked Mr. Seselj to proceed, but I've been thinking, and I'm a bit surprised at your answer. I would like to have -- let's move to private session very briefly. Mr. Registrar, could we please move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you said that the Serbs had been talked into leaving --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you said that Serbs had been talked into leaving, are you referring to 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what year it was, but they were on the move. I have a videocassette showing that, a speech made by a distinguished gentleman who was instigating people to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can a distinguished gentleman make several hundred thousand Serbs leave Zagreb, Rijeka, Varazdin, and many other Croatian cities and have these people take their women and children and leave practically everything that they had acquired during the course of their life? Who could do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Force is the distinguished gentleman I referred to, and I will put that under quotation marks. However, these people would not want to leave on their own just as the Croats didn't want to leave. It was simply force major. One had to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So someone forced these Serbs to leave? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If so many of them had left, it would be very surprising that it was voluntary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know that the first Serbs started leaving when the Tudjman regime came to power; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not blaming anyone. I'm not approving of anything as far as the situation is concerned, but evil things happened on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we do agree that evil things happened on both sides. Now, let us discuss where it was first that the evil cropped up and where it was worse in terms of their consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I am the one who should speak of that least of all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you should not speak about this, then we're not going to dwell on it any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a question. You said that they were convinced by speeches; but according to you, who convinced them? Is it the Croatian authorities or other entities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said to Mr. Vojvoda Seselj that it's not for me to say who had made the call. I personally have a video-recording of the gentleman's speech, and what was said was that people should be on the move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you just said "Vojvoda Seselj." Why are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session. Could we please redact, Mr. Registrar. I tried to stop you, but you were faster than I was. So you're saying that you're using "vojvoda" because that is what is relayed in the press. Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness says "vojvoda" because I really am a Chetnik vojvoda, and I'm proud of that title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. VS-0061, now we're going to deal with the first rally of the Serb Radical Party in Hrtkovci on the 6th of May, 1991. You were not present at that rally, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is only from other persons that you heard that some things had been mentioned during the rally; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact -- or rather, do you remember that this rally was held within the pre-election campaign for the first federal elections in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia towards the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People I socialised with told me that your purpose was to establish your party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To establish a branch of the Serb Radical Party in Hrtkovci and to make a pre-election speech, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who attended the rally, did they tell you that I was presenting the election programme of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and among the many things that I was told, I remembered many good things as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I talked about economics, social, cultural programmes, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in passing, I spoke of the ethnic issue, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was mentioned as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you did not attend the rally - but you did read the newspapers and you watched television; you listened to the radio - I assume that you'd have to remember had I during this election campaign presented two theses. The first one, due to the fact that Tudjman's Croatian authorities had expelled thousands of Serbs from Croatia, I attacked the regime in Serbia because it did not carry out measures of retorsion. "Retorsion" means retaliation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have an administrative question. I noted that in Binder -- in the Prosecution's Binder number 3, there is -- we can find your speech, the speech you gave. And if I'm right, this speech comes from a book that was published by the Serbian Radical Party. In the documents in Cyrillic, we have this speech, and this speech is translated into English in the Prosecution's binder. Given that this speech is extremely important, the judgement will be made in French, and I don't want to run any risk as to a possible misinterpretation of the words you used in your speech, so this will have to be really very carefully translated. I checked and wondered whether I could obtain a French translation -- a perfect French translation of this speech that's in Cyrillic from CLSS. I was told that here we don't translate from B/C/S into French. We translate from B/C/S into English and then the English is translated into French, so we do have a problem here. The head of the CLSS -- the head of the department --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- speaks all three languages and can control what is being translated, but as of now, we don't have a translation. B/C/S into French, you know, that would be 100-per cent perfect. Maybe given your resources and what means you have at your disposal, maybe you could obtain a French translation using the services of a Serbian official translator who could actually do the job. Here at the Tribunal, we don't go directly from B/C/S into French for written translations. I wanted you to be aware of this so you know exactly what the situation is. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I wanted to note that the publication of Mr. Seselj's book containing text from the speech is not contemporaneous, nor is it necessarily a verbatim recording. He has published the speech in two different books. One indicates a stoppage of a tape and an incomplete recording, so I just wanted to qualify that it is some evidence of the speech but certainly not conclusive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That is very important. Thank you. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor after this digression.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this speech was first published in a book of mine before there was any intimation that an indictment would be issued against me in The Hague, so what is recorded on videocassette was recorded on paper too. If this witness has a videocassette of the speech, it would be a good thing if it were to be brought here because no one could have known then that it would be needed one day to have it broadcast in its entirety. What is clear from the speech is that I did not read any list or name any names, and in the indictment it says that I made lists and named names. So some things are clear already. As for the translation of this speech into French, the Registry would have to take care of that. I don't have the resources or the possibilities to do that. Unfortunately, I had a good lawyer who had a very good knowledge of French. He was on my team. Dragan Tasic was his name. Regrettably, he died a few months ago. He provided invaluable assistance to me when I needed to have some things translated from French. You remember when I cross-examined Yves Tomic, that Prosecution expert witness, that I then had text in the French language thanks to Dragan Tasic, that associate of mine. He died a premature death, and I cannot deal with the French language any longer. At any rate, I have to ask this witness about some things that have to do with that speech. The witness already confirmed that in May I had already publicly advocated retorsion and I attacked the regime in Serbia for not carrying it out. It is retaliation, actually. If the Croatian authorities were expelling Serbs from Croatia, I was attacking the Milosevic regime for not responding the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true, but why do the innocent have to suffer? Who was innocent there? Your people and my people. This is a sin that will have to be atoned for. No comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I fully understand you, but in that situation that was one of the solutions to an already existing problem; don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Regrettably, it was one of the solutions when there wasn't a better one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a more normal situation, it wouldn't have crossed anyone's mind to advocate that kind of thing, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank God.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But by then, hundreds of thousands of expelled Serbs had reached Serbia. In that unbearable situation, this came up as one of the possible solutions by itself, although it is painful. I agree that it's painful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is painful, but the question is that someone had to instigate all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know who instigated all that: the Tudjman regime in Croatia. Isn't that right? There is no one else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say anything. I'm not involved in politics. We are a smart people. Let us read people's minds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Witness, could you please specify this for us? You said that you did not hear the speech directly. You heard about it. I would like to know whether you were told that in this speech there was hints at retorsion or retaliation measures, retaliation, which is the word used by Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would see two or three people at a time, at the most. They were visibly frightened, and they said, "Sir, we have to leave." I don't want to state in public anything that I had heard from other people. I already said I'm not interested in that speech. However, they left, saying that they felt that they needed to leave as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who attended the rally, did they tell you that at one point in time during this speech, I stated that when the Serb Radical Party comes to power, we would resolve that problem more easily; we are going to give expelled Serbs Croat addresses, and we're going to say, "Go there and exchange property with these people"? Did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did tell me that, and I found it in many newspapers, and this became extremely popular among the Serbs who had come from Croatia - you did - and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that I'm not denying the fact that I advocated such political positions at all? I confirm this to this day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a civilised way, you were sharply against both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say in one of your statements that I mentioned some names during the rally; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Names? That was never uttered by me. I heard things from other people, and I said that I don't want to speak about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other people told you that I mentioned the names of some Croats from Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, including my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who mentioned your name and in what context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When names are mentioned, tensions run even higher and the pressure is even greater. We were pressured to leave as soon as possible. That was their conclusion, not my personal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ms. Dahl, maybe you could explain your reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: May we discuss this in closed session so we don't increase the amount of redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few seconds, then, now. Mr. Registrar, could we please briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: (redacted) It's difficult for you, I know. We all make mistakes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Mate Markus is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I know all of these people to this day. We socialise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what is the truth? Who knows whether this is true or not? I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: May we go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know what? If these names were uttered in 1992, then everybody remembers that, I guess, and it is well known which names were uttered, but it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. VS-0061, since at the time of the rally of the Serbian Radical Party you were in Hrtkovci, did you hear that there was no incident whatsoever at the rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that everything was conducted in a civilised, orderly manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that a lot of Croats attended the rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They couldn't have liked my words concerning Croats and Croatia, but perhaps they liked some other things that I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both are true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a large number of people from the neighbouring villages there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that because so many people could not have come just from Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during that campaign, we didn't have time to tour all places in Serbia. We just selected certain places, and then we would call people from neighbouring villages; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what it seems like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were people from Mikinavci [phoen], Paticova [phoen], and some other places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, even from the south of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean from the other bank of the Sava River; that's what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the vicinity of Sabac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, because Sabac is just across over the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you challenge the figure. He says that there were 100, approximately. Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In examination-in-chief, you stated that the greatest wave of departures of Croats from Hrtkovci came after the killing of Mijat Stefanac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Stefanac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After your speech and especially after the killing of Mr. Stefanac, the number of people departing increased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The murder of Stefanac was almost two months after my speech, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if that was May, then two months later, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated to The Hague investigators that the murder of Stefanac has not been resolved to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, whether it has been resolved or not. I heard that some people were accused. Now, whether it was fully resolved, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, but that's not what your statement says. Let's see what your statement says. Paragraph 32 of your statement which you gave in 2006, would you please put it on the ELMO? It's very important. There's just one sentence there but quite remarkable. Could that be placed on the ELMO, please. If not, we'd rather not waste time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The image must not be broadcast outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 32 of your 2006 statement. This is page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm unclear about the display on the ELMO. Everyone has a copy of the statement in the courtroom, I believe, and the witness can look at his text, but putting it on the document camera is designed to broadcast it. So I'm a little confused and would like to ask for some clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theoretically, the Registrar can stop or prevent the picture from being broadcast. There seems to be a problem because we don't have it on our screens. Since everyone has a paper copy, put your question, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 32 of your 2006 statement, there is just one sentence: "The murder of Mijat Stefanac was never solved." Correct? Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, Mr. Seselj. I can see that. As far as I'm aware, it hasn't been solved. If it has been, then I beg everybody's forgiveness, but I'm unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a whole set of documents here. I published them in my book (redacted) I'm not going to put the entire book to you. We will simply see from these documents that the murderers of Stefanac were arrested on the same day and tried later on. This is the first set of documents starting on page 6, the documents that I had photocopied today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: In January, the Chamber redacted the title of the book because of its offensive nature, and I would ask that that same decision be repeated today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber does not want to hear such offensive words. In the interest of justice and in the interest of persons, I would like to ask you not to use such offensive, inappropriate terms.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm not attributing anything to anyone. What I said was quite appropriate. This is the correct title of the book. I can't change the title now after it's been published in 3.000 copies and then several thousand more copies were downloaded from my web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the title of the book in a number of countries would have been subject to a legal action to ban such titles being used because of the terms used. I don't know what's happened as far as the interested party is concerned. Maybe she did not resort to any legal action. Whatever the case may be, this Tribunal cannot use such offensive terms, and I would adopt the same view if the situation were the other way around. Let's now focus on matters of substance and hear your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please place on the ELMO - all of these documents can be shown to the public because they deal with the murder of Mijat Stefanac - just to describe briefly how this all unfolded and so that you can give me your position on that. Do you have this set of documents? I provided them today so that they can be photocopied for everybody, including OTP and the Trial Chamber. It's the first set of documents and then the second subset within the first set, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that this is Mr. Seselj's first time conducting a trial, but the vague references to the material without numbering or date or further reference leaves me unable to identify what he's referring to, particularly because I can't read the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, when you introduce a document, say, for instance, that this is an article from the press published on such-and-such a day, stemming from such-and-such a newspaper or review, so please give us a number, and then everybody understands. I've seen a number of newspaper articles pass before my eyes, but just specify that you are placing such-and-such a document on the ELMO. Give us a place, name, and date of the article. This avoids the Prosecution from getting on its feet, and we save time thereby.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am putting to the witness the official note of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, Sremska Mitrovica SUP, dated 29th of June, 1992, compiled by Milorad Popovic, authorised official -- police official. And if we show it to Mr. Stefanac [as interpreted], then with his assistance we can learn of the contents of this document. When he sees it, when we put it on the ELMO and he will tell us about it, then you will learn what's in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are quite right. However, you could have supplemented this by saying that this document was given to you by the Ministry of the Interior, you had asked to have a copy from them, and you could have got up and said, "This is a forged document," and so on and so forth. So you have to tell us what the source of this document is, whether it comes from the archives, your lawyers, or whoever may have given you these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm convinced that the Prosecution has had this material for quite a long time, but that's not the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have this document before you now, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I still don't have it on my screen. Oh, there it is. All right. Do you see that this is the official note of the Sremska Mitrovica SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want me to read this, this first sentence, or would you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the first sentence: "On the 29th of June, 1992, after the person suspected of the murder of Mijat Stefanac from Hrtkovci were taken in - namely, Mladjen Kekerovic, Momcilo Vidakovic, Branislav Kalinic, Pero Lukac, Petar Zagarac, and Dragan Lazarevic - these persons have been processed in the Crime Investigation Department. Their clothes were checked, as there was a suspicion that on the trousers of Mladjen Kekerovic as well T-shirt of Momcilo Vidakovic, there are blood traces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't need to go on further. Since Stefanac was killed on the night between the 28th and 29th of June, isn't it clear that immediately on the following day, the 29th of June, the policemen from Sremska Mitrovica arrested six perpetrators of this crime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This murder took place between St. Vitas's day and St. Peter's Day, and I see from the documents that this was done, but I didn't know about this earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document now. We see here that Mladjen Kekerovic is being sent to detention. You see the text down there. Perhaps I'll read it. Perhaps I can read it faster, and then you can confirm whether I'm reading right or not. There is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note: It is too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Reading the document would put the interpreters behind, and I cannot follow without the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please try and slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's not read it, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see in the first sentence that Mladjen Kekerovic is being sent to detention because he had killed Mijat Stefanac from Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no mention of Kekerovic here. There is Vidakovic, Momcilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look up there below the heading "Rjesenje," "Decision." It says Mladjen Kekerovic, and then further down it says that he did it together with Momcilo Vidakovic, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see the name of Kekerovic anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see "Rjesenje" up on the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes. Sorry, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is a decision stating that Kekerovic, Mladjen, is being detained; and then further down, Vidakovic, Momcilo, is being named as an accomplice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see all of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the next document now, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pero Lukac is also sent to detention. Do you see his name here underneath the word "Decision"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the disposition is somewhat different because this is the crime of violence imperilling the rights of citizens, so he is a participant in the violence that preceded the killing. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next page now. Dragan Lazarevic was also detained. Do you have the other page on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the papers before you? Can you please be so kind as to leaf through it yourself so that we don't have to keep calling the lady in all the time? She can put it all in front of you, and then you can just leaf through it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we have a decision on the detention of Dragan Lazarevic, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the disposition down here says why it is that he was detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we've seen all these documents. What the Chamber is interested in is this : Whether after the investigation there was a trial or not. This is what matters to us, so -- whether the perpetrators of the murder were tried and convicted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you're so impatient, Mr. President, I have the judgement. If you leaf through these documents, then you will see that, again, there is a decision on detention, and then there is an on-site investigation report, and then the judgement, which is page 16 in this set of documents. This is the judgement of the District Court in Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it, Mr. VS-0061? Have you found the judgement on page 16? It says "16," and there is a handwritten numeral.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't find it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The lady will help you. Page 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Witness. Stop. We were in open session, so we'll have to redact some portions. I asked you not to mention any names, nor to tell us what you do in life. We are in open session. We shall redact this. We can make up for the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found page 16, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. "In the name of the people..."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. "In the name of the people..." and then the judgement is handed down. And then it says that the accused, Mladjen Kekerovic, and then his information follows, correct? And then the second accused, Momcilo Vidakovic, and then his personal details, and then the personal details of the rest of the four accused, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have something concerning Mladjen Kekerovic. He is guilty because on the 28th of June, 1992, having arrived in his vehicle, Mercedes license plates, to Nikinci, to -- with Mijat Stefanac, for some reason they were travelling in the car together, weren't they? And since Stefanac asked him to drive him from Hrtkovci to Nikinci, and then they went to a bar and they drank in a bar, and then there was a brawl in the bar, and then -- please go to page 19, the handwritten 19 numeral. And then it says that he is guilty of manslaughter -- of manslaughter. This was a murder committed in a brawl between two people who were drunk, and he was sentenced to four years and six months in prison, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's guilty of unlawful possession of weapon -- unlicensed possession of weapon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: For the Chamber's convenience, I have the 1992 indictment, the 1992 judgement of conviction, and the 1995 Supreme Court confirmation of convictions for the crime of violence related to an ethnic group. I have them in translation and wanted to tender. I made copies. I didn't know if this was going to come up in cross-examination, but I have a full set for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness: Sir, do you know these people who were convicted for the manslaughter of Mr. Stefanac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I saw them, but I personally don't know them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you happen to know their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So they were members of the Serb community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They come from the Serbian nation, Serbian community.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Harhoff, if I can assist you, these people are not from Hrtkovci. They came to Hrtkovci on some business, and they met with Stefanac. They wanted to sell a vehicle, and then they got drunk in a bar and started arguing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yeah. I was just trying to establish the ethnicity because I think this is an issue which obviously is of some importance to this question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me get to the point. With these documents, we have seen that those people who had killed Stefanac were tried, and this was confirmed in 1995 by the Supreme Court. Now, when you are interviewed by the OTP in 2006, in paragraph 32 you say that the murder was never resolved. So I'm dumbstruck by this because there was a trial, people were convicted, and judgements were handed down. The investigator, if he'd done his job properly, should have known that an investigation had been carried out and a judgement had been rendered. So when you discussed this murder with the investigator, the investigator knew nothing about this? Didn't the name ring a bell? What do you remember? Because you, in your position, maybe you didn't know that the perpetrators had been apprehended and convicted, but the investigator according to his mandate must prepare a perfect case file, that he discussed the issue of this murder without mentioning anything that had happened and let you say that the murder had never been resolved, I must say I am a little surprised by this. When you were in contact with the investigator, do you remember anything? When you said this, sir, didn't he say anything and he just moved on to paragraph 32? Do you remember anything about this? Because when we read paragraph 30, 31, and 32, something is being demonstrated here, and there is a demonstration. And when there's been a judgement, well, the two don't really tally. Do you remember what the investigator told you at the time, or was it just plain sailing and nobody noticed anything? And these were high-profile investigators. Do you remember anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, I found out that some persons had been convicted. I was not aware of the names. Among all of these people, one of the guilty parties was convicted as well. As for the killing of Mr. Stefanac, I was not aware of the fact that the case had been resolved altogether. I had begged for forgiveness a few moments ago. I did not know myself that it was a solved murder case and that the murderer had been convicted, and then the gentleman from The Hague Tribunal just stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you learned about it, but when? Before 2006? When did you find out that someone had been convicted for this murder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned about it in 2004. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You learned about it in 2004. But when you're saying that the murder was not solved, that's not true. When someone is convicted, the murder has been solved. So why do we have this sentence in your statement? When you read -- when you reread your statement, it says the murder was never solved. Obviously, it doesn't tally.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg for forgiveness. I have already said that I'm glad that it was resolved. However, I was ignorant of this. I thought that it had not been solved. I made a mistake, and I kindly ask the Trial Chamber for forgiveness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one last question. You know, I could go on for hours, but I have one last question. When you signed your statement in your own language, handed to you in your own language, did you very carefully reread all sentences? Did you go -- scrutinize every word, every sentence before signing, or were you just handed the statement and you just signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement was read out before me, all of it, and I signed it without having a single document. They didn't give me a single document for keep. What I signed at that moment I believed was the most sincere thing possible. However, there seems to be this omission, and I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the interpreter read the English version, and you listened to it, and then you signed. Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you know how much I abhor closed sessions, but the question that I'm about to put now is one that you will probably say can reveal the witness's identity, so I'd like to draw your attention to that fact in advance. The question that follows is a question like that, but I would be the happiest of all if the witness had not sought protective measures. So -- well, perhaps you'll consider this question to be one that merits private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move into private session. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, you may leave. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're now in open session. The Registrar is going to raise the blinds. It would be nice to have a remote to do that. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I rise to my feet simply to ask for an extension of the word limit with respect to the Prosecution's response to Mr. Seselj's submission number 394. I believe, if memory serves me, that response was 5.000 -- or that motion was 5.650 words. We would ask, respectfully, for a similar word limit in order to file our response. That would be point number 1. Point number 2. It is my understanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Let me consult with my colleagues on this one. I'm in favour of this, and on behalf of the Trial Chamber I grant you this motion. So you can exceed the word limit. But let me tell you, as I already said, I always grant these types of motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And we are always grateful for that, Mr. President. The second request would be concerning the same response. It's my understanding that our response is due today. I would ask that we be given one additional day. If that's acceptable, we will file that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let me consult with my colleagues. Yes. There, again, we grant your motion. We understand that you are running into a lot of difficulties to be on time, and we grant you this extension.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, finally, as indicated earlier this week, tomorrow I will be circulating by way of e-mail the updated list of witnesses that remain to be called. What I have done is placed all of the information on one table rather than two but made an indication that's clearly marked on the document, and it's a self-explanatory document. And that will be distributed no later than the close of business tomorrow. There are no additional changes with respect to the witness calender for next week, so I would propose that I not recirculate that. The calender as it was circulated last Friday remains in effect at least with respect to next week, but I will be circulating the revised or updated witness list tomorrow, and we will be responding to Dr. Seselj's submission 394 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, it would be nice if we had a colour chart because that way, you know, we can make a difference between viva voce witnesses and the 92 ter witnesses, and a colourful life is more pleasant than a sad and black-and-white life. So please put some colour into your chart, if you may. I know that you can do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's absolutely in living colour, Your Honours, and you'll have that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As for next week, Monday there's no hearing; Tuesday is a holiday, so we will only be sitting for two days, Wednesday and Thursday. We're sitting in the afternoon. Furthermore, how long have you set aside for the examination-in-chief of this witness? Two hours equals a day, after all. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hope that you will make a record of when I showed goodwill and that when I need time, in turn you would be just as generous towards my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I never doubted your goodwill to make sure that these hearings run smoothly. It was almost time to adjourn. I now wish everyone a good afternoon. I want to thank Mr. Seselj's associates for having come to this hearing. I hope that their financial -- the financial problems will find a solution as quickly as possible so that we can see you again very soon in this courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 1st day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.09 p.m.,
